owner_creation.analysis: The meta_escape pointer initially borrows the static backslash string; -e chooses a static empty string or argument tail, and -f selects meta_escape_buf.
owner_creation.invariant: Escape storage is borrowed from one of three live owners.
limitations: meta_escape may borrow a literal, argument tail or meta_escape_buf.

aliases_escapes.analysis: meta_escape borrows a static literal, the two-byte static array or an argv tail owned by args_strings throughout main_0.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Escape borrows remain inside the argument owner lifetime.
limitations: Private single-invocation helper state only; metachars heap ownership and lstrtol arithmetic remain separate pending entries.
Its raw C pointer must not outlive the selected backing owner.

callback_targets.analysis: strlen and printf read meta_escape synchronously as string data; the pointer is never registered as executable code.
callback_targets.invariant: Escape strings cannot act as callback addresses.
limitations: Direct printf/string reads assume a stable NUL-terminated backing region.

invalidation.analysis: Later options may replace the meta_escape pointer before output; no code retains an earlier escape alias and the backing argv Vecs are not resized in main_0.
invalidation.invariant: Pointer replacement occurs before escape readers run.

mutation_commit.analysis: meta_escape is assigned either a borrowed option tail or the address of meta_escape_buf after its two bytes are written. The pointer has no separate length field to commit, and its C-string lifetime depends on retaining the selected argument or static buffer until helper exit.
mutation_commit.invariant: The escape pointer always selects a terminated string.

release_pair.analysis: The meta_escape pointer is non-owning and never freed; args_strings owns argv storage while literals and meta_escape_buf have image lifetime.
release_pair.invariant: Escape pointers must not be passed to free.
limitations: meta_escape must not be freed when it points into argv or static bytes.

error_cleanup.analysis: A missing -f number exits before output, so partially changed option state is not consumed; other parse errors do not transfer meta_escape's owner.
error_cleanup.invariant: Option failure cannot publish a dangling escape borrow.

signals_handoff.analysis: The single helper invocation has no signal handler that changes meta_escape; SIGPIPE may terminate output without replacing its owner.
signals_handoff.invariant: Escape configuration is stable during output.
